data.title: Small- and mid-cap funds retain folio lead despite sharp October slowdown
data.description:
Small- and mid-cap (SMID) funds continued to account for the bulk of folio additions in the active equity category in October, even as the pace of new additions nearly halved from the previous month amid a correction in the broader market.
 
The two categories together accounted for 56.9 per cent of active equity folio additions in October, marginally lower than 57.9 per cent in September. This was despite the combined additions declining 47.4 per cent to 539,000 from 1 million a month earlier.
 
The net inflows into the two categories also plunged last month. They garnered net inflows of ₹11,300 crore in October, down 33 per cent from the all-time high of ₹16,873 crore in September. The decline in folio growth as well as net inflows came as the broader market corrected for the second consecutive month in October. The Nifty Smallcap 250 declined almost 6 per cent, while the Nifty Midcap 150 slipped almost 4 per cent last month. In comparison, the Nifty 50 gained about 2 per cent.
 
 
The data highlights that small- and mid-cap funds remain key to mutual fund (MF) folio growth. Experts say that the higher investor interest in the two categories stems from expectations of better performance, and the trend can reverse only if large-caps deliver sustained outperformance.
 
"We see two likely reasons for the strong share of new folios in small- and mid-cap funds. The first is the expectation of faster earnings growth. Investors see room for smaller businesses to expand into new markets and gain market share as they grow. The second factor is relative performance. Over the past year, small- and mid-cap funds have generally compared favourably with large-cap funds," said Sorbh Gupta, head of equities, Bajaj Asset Management.
 
"If large-cap funds sustain a period of stronger relative performance, they could begin to attract a higher share of new folios," he added.
 
The outperformance of small- and mid-caps in the past three-four years has resulted in sharp growth in folios as well as the assets under management (AUM) of schemes focusing on these segments.
 
Within the equity category, small-cap and sectoral/thematic funds recorded the fastest growth over the seven-year period between October 2019 and October 2026. Small-cap AUM expanded 9.2 times at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 37.3 per cent, while sectoral/thematic funds grew 8.3 times at a CAGR of 35.3 per cent. Large- and mid-cap funds and mid-cap funds also recorded strong CAGRs of 30.2 per cent and 29.6 per cent, respectively, ICRA Analytics stated in its recent report.

data.title: Trai extends 1601 numbering series to consumer-facing sectors in Phase 2
data.description:
India’s telecom regulator on Friday extended the use of the 1601 numbering series to consumer-facing services, including retail chains, e-commerce, commercial airlines, ride-hailing and food aggregator apps, travel agencies, and telecom service providers, among others.
 
In its directions, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) said the 1601 series would be available for service and transactional voice calls to these additional sectors under the second phase, which will help consumers identify legitimate calls and prevent fraud and impersonation.
 
“Being a trusted channel, the numbers from this series are allocated only to the verified entities, and thereby helping consumers to easily identify legitimate service and transactional calls. This measure is an important tool in combating impersonation by fraudsters who use normal 10-digit numbers and falsely claim to represent legitimate businesses,” Trai said.
  
In the first phase that began in August this year, the 1601 series was made available to electricity distribution companies, water utilities, city gas distribution companies, LPG distributors, and other utility service providers. Courier, express logistics, parcel delivery, freight, and logistics companies engaged in delivering consignments were also eligible for the series.
 
Trai had earlier mandated the use of the 1600 series for service and transaction-related calls by banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI) entities and for government-to-citizen communication. The series was introduced in January 2026. Entities cannot make promotional calls from the numbering series.
 
In the second phase, Trai said that the 1601 series would be used by retail chains, e-commerce companies, hospitals, diagnostic laboratories, telecom service providers, internet service providers, automobile sales, repair and servicing businesses, travel agencies, commercial airlines, food aggregators, ride-hailing aggregators, and lending service providers. “Only the entities having an annual turnover of ₹500 crore or more in at least one of the preceding three financial years shall be eligible,” the regulator specified.
 
Distribution platform operators such as direct-to-home, headend-in-the-sky, internet protocol television (IPTV) service providers, and multi-system operators having a subscriber base of 1 million or more in any month during the preceding 12 months would also be eligible.
 
“The 1601-series numbers shall be assigned only to the companies registered in India under the applicable law,” the regulator added.
 
Telcos have been directed to complete the onboarding and migration of all eligible entities within 180 days, and they will have to publicise the availability of the series among eligible entities, submit status reports to Trai every 15 days, and submit a final compliance report after 6.5 months. “Based on a review of the implementation, the Authority may notify additional sectors or eligible entities from time to time,” the regulator added.

data.title: India's forex reserves fall $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion on gold losses
data.description:
India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion during the week ended November 20, according to the latest data from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
The total reserves stood at $705.34 billion in the previous week ended November 13.
 
Foreign currency assets (FCAs), the largest component of the reserves, declined by $266 million to $583.19 billion during the reported week. FCAs, expressed in dollar terms, include the effect of appreciation or depreciation of non-US currencies such as the euro, pound, and yen held in the reserves.
 
Gold reserves declined by $4.10 billion to $94.52 billion during the reported week, while special drawing rights (SDRs) fell by $67 million to $18.45 billion. India's reserve position with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) fell by $15 million to $4.74 billion, the RBI data showed.
 
 
The total reserves are now about $84.8 billion below the all-time high of $785.7 billion touched in the week ended September 4, after significant foreign currency inflows through a special concessional swap scheme for diaspora deposits. The previous week's fall of $14.21 billion had been driven mainly by revaluation losses, led by gold reserves, which declined by $6.18 billion.

data.title: UK study visa refusals hit 11-year high, Indian student grants fall 29%
data.description:
The refusal rate for UK sponsored study visas has risen to its highest level in 11 years, while the number of visas granted to Indian students has fallen by 29%, adding to concerns over the country's declining appeal among international students.
 
Home Office figures released on November 26 show that the UK granted 335,801 sponsored study visas in the year ending September 2026, down 23% from the previous year. The number is 49% below the peak recorded in the year ending June 2023.
 
Applications from main applicants fell 20% over the year, while applications between July and September stood at 230,300, down 16% from the corresponding period a year earlier.
  
According to an analysis of the data by Higher Insights and The Admit, the refusal rate reached 6.4% in the year ending September 2026, the highest rolling annual rate since September 2015. Withdrawals before a decision also increased by more than 370% during the peak autumn quarter.
 
Indian student visa grants fall 29%
 
India remained the UK's second-largest source of sponsored international students, accounting for 69,855 visa grants, or 22% of the total, in the year ending September 2026. This represented a 29% decline from the previous year.
 
China topped the list with 80,932 grants, accounting for 25% of the total. Nigeria recorded 19,734 grants, down 34% year on year. Grants to Pakistani and Nepali students fell by 72% and 22%, respectively.
 
The decline was particularly pronounced among students pursuing postgraduate education. Visas granted for master's-level courses fell 29% to 181,920, accounting for 58% of all sponsored study visa grants, compared with 63% a year earlier.
 
Visas granted to dependants also declined, falling 33% to 13,514.
 
Fewer international students moving into work
 
The decline is also extending to post-study work opportunities. Extensions under the Graduate Route, which allows eligible international graduates to remain in the UK to work or look for employment, fell 31% to 162,881.
 
Indian nationals accounted for the largest number of Graduate Route extensions, with 66,552, followed by Pakistani nationals at 24,768 and Nigerians at 20,478.
 
The Home Office's Migrant Journey report shows that 41% of people who entered the UK on study visas in 2020 still held valid leave or indefinite leave to remain at the end of 2025. Of this group, 26% had moved to a work visa route.
 
Tighter compliance rules for universities
 
The decline in student numbers comes as the UK government tightens requirements for universities sponsoring international students.
 
New guidance introduced in June 2026 strengthened the Basic Compliance Assessment (BCA), requiring institutions to keep their student visa refusal rate below 5%, maintain a course enrolment rate of at least 95% and achieve a course completion rate of at least 85%. The minimum course completion threshold is due to rise to 90% in June 2027.
 
The Home Office said continued credibility checks and stricter expectations on universities to admit only genuine students had prompted some institutions to reduce sponsorship in certain countries.
 
Russell Group warns of economic impact
 
The fall in international student numbers is damaging universities, the UK economy and the country's global influence, the Russell Group, which represents some of Britain's leading universities, warned on Thursday.
 
Zaid Kadhum, policy manager at the Russell Group, said several years of policy changes had reduced demand for British higher education.
 
“This is damaging universities, the UK’s soft power, and the economy,” he said in a press release.
 
Kadhum said international students supported local jobs and businesses while helping British universities compete globally. He also raised concerns about rising visa refusal rates.
 
“A robust immigration system is in everyone’s interests, but decisions must be fair and transparent, and we should be careful not to deter genuine students in the process,” he said.
 
The Russell Group has urged the government to provide universities with greater policy stability so that institutions can plan ahead and continue attracting students from overseas.
 
The decline comes amid tighter immigration rules for international students. In January 2024, the previous Conservative government introduced restrictions barring most international students from bringing dependants to the UK.
 
UK net migration falls to lowest level since 1997
 
The warning comes as the UK records a sharp fall in net migration. Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Thursday welcomed the latest figures, while saying Brexit had done nothing to improve border control.
 
Net migration fell to an estimated 77,000 in the year ending June 2026, its lowest level since 1997, excluding the Covid-19 pandemic, according to provisional estimates released by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) on November 26. This was a 62% decline from 204,000 in the previous year.
 
The ONS said arrivals of non-EU+ nationals for study-related reasons fell by 33,000 compared with the previous year. Meanwhile, 292,000 non-EU+ nationals left the UK during the year, with around 53% having originally entered on study-related visas.

data.title: Crop insurance claims set for multi-year high as weather losses mount
data.description:
Crop insurance claims for the Kharif 2026 season are expected to exceed premiums collected, with insurers anticipating this to be one of the worst ever periods in the sector due to prolonged dry spells, uneven rainfall, and cyclonic activity that hit agricultural production across several states.
 
The industry's loss ratio — which measures claims as a proportion of premiums — is expected to be well above 100 per cent, making the current Kharif season one of the most challenging for crop insurers in the past eight to nine years, according to early industry estimates. However, they expect the claims picture to become clearer by the end of November or early December.
 
According to insurance brokers, the season could be comparable to 2015-16, when India experienced a super El Niño and the agriculture sector experienced severe losses, following which the government launched a crop insurance scheme named 'Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)'.
 
“(The) Industry is expecting losses worth thousands of crore in crop insurance this time, while the premiums charged were nearly 50 per cent less than last year due to better claims experience in the previous season,” an insurer said.
 
Prolonged dry spells during August and September, particularly in rain-deficient regions, have affected crop production across several key states. Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh are among the major states facing the impact of El Niño conditions, while Haryana and Andhra Pradesh are also likely to see elevated claims.
 
The low rainfall situation has added to the pressure, with several agricultural regions across Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Assam and the Northeast experiencing varying degrees of moisture stress. October's cyclonic activity has also contributed to higher claims in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
 
According to PMFBY portal, the gross premium collected for kharif season in FY26 stood at ₹12,261.68 crore, nearly 15 per cent less than the premiums collected last year, while the sum insured increased by 26 per cent to ₹1.83 trillion.
 
Under the PMFBY, the sum insured for a farmer is determined by the scale of finance per hectare for a specific crop, as decided by the District-Level Technical Committee and pre-declared by the State-Level Committee. The total sum insured is calculated by multiplying the scale of finance by the area of the notified crop proposed to be insured.
 
Farmers pay relatively low premiums under the scheme — up to 2 per cent of the sum insured for kharif crops, up to 1.5 per cent for rabi crops, and up to 5 per cent for commercial and horticultural crops. The balance premium is shared equally by the Centre and state governments, except in the north-eastern states (from kharif 2020) and Himalayan states (from kharif 2023), where the sharing ratio is 90:10. Farmers are not required to pay any premium beyond these prescribed rates.
 
The PMFBY operational guidelines also provide for three alternative risk-transfer structures besides the standard model: cup-and-cap (80:110), cup-and-cap (60:130), and a profit-and-loss-sharing model. Under these structures, if claims remain below specified thresholds, a portion of the premium subsidy paid by the government is returned to the state treasury.
 
According to Rohit Boda, group managing director at the JB Boda Group, it is still early to arrive at a final picture of claims for the 2026 kharif season, but indicators so far point to a difficult year for the crop insurance market.
 
“Premium rates have also come down this year, which is another factor influencing the claims outlook. Overall, crop insurance premium rates have declined by approximately 36 per cent. The reduction has been particularly noticeable in states of Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Jharkhand, following the fresh tenders issued in 2026,” he said
 
According to Mohammad Faizan Huq, associate president and head of Agriculture, Parametric and A&H, and Reinsurance at Howden India, the overall premium collected under the PMFBY and the Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) for the current kharif season is provisionally estimated at around ₹12,250 crore, more than 13 per cent lower than the previous season.
 
He added that according to early industry indications the all-India Kharif season's loss ratio (claims over premium) is expected to be well beyond 100 per cent. The loss ratio may vary with insurers depending upon their exposure in states where production losses are higher.
 
According to experts, lower rates were quoted by insurers in key states, including Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Karnataka. Insurers have also reduced the premium pool even as weather-related risks have increased, putting pressure on underwriting performance.
 
The claims experience is expected to be more challenging than last year, when the kharif season's claims ratio was around 90-100 per cent. The final claims liability for the current season, however, will depend on yield data emerging from field-level Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) and estimates generated through the YES-Tech system, or Yield Estimation System based on Technology.
 
Insurers are currently assessing crop losses, with the final claims numbers likely to emerge as state governments complete yield assessments and submit the necessary data. The wider coverage reflects increased participation in the scheme even as insurers brace for a difficult claims season, with the combination of lower premiums and higher weather-related losses likely to weigh on the industry's performance.

data.title: RBI cuts CRR maintenance requirement for banks back to 90% from Dec 1
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India on Friday cut the minimum cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement for banks back to 90 per cent, amid a decline in the surplus liquidity in the banking system. 
In October this year, the central bank had hiked the CRR maintenance requirement to 99 per cent from the earlier 90 per cent amid a liquidity surplus. 
"On the basis of an assessment of the current and evolving macroeconomic situation and liquidity conditions, it has been decided to reduce the minimum daily maintenance of the cash reserve ratio (CRR) from 99 per cent of the requirement to 90 per cent, effective from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026," a central bank notification said. 
 
CRR is the quantum of deposits which banks have to park with the RBI. Banks do not earn any returns on the money set aside for CRR, and the ratio currently stands at 3 per cent of their deposits. 
The move comes days after the banking system liquidity turned to deficit for the first time in five months on the back of Goods and Services Tax outflows and the RBI's foreign exchange market interventions.

data.title: OTT releases this week: Hanuman Ansh, Spider-Man and more to watch online
data.description:
The final week of November brings a mix of Bollywood thrillers, Hollywood superhero films, science-fiction dramas and Korean romantic series to OTT platforms. From the much-awaited spiritual biopic, Hanuman Ansh, among the key Indian releases, Spider-Man: Brand New Day adds superhero shows to the lineup. 
 
Several OTT platforms featured in this week's streaming schedule arriving in the last week of November 2026 are returning with new stories, along with a few interesting titles for viewers who enjoy multiple genres.

Top 5 OTT releases to watch online this week

Hanuman Ansh
 
Release Date: November 27/November 29
 
Platform: SonyLIV, Netflix
 
Hanuman Ansh is a Hindi spiritual drama drawn from the experiences and lessons of the popular Neem Karoli Baba, commonly referred to as Maharaj-ji. Under the direction of Vishal Chaturvedi, the movie tells the story of a young boy who sets off on a spiritual journey that ultimately guides him to embrace a life filled with belief, kindness, and selfless service.
 
 
Spider-Man: Brand New Day
 
Reported Release Date: November 26
 
Platform: Netflix
 
Spider-Man: Brand New Day centers on Peter Parker as he adjusts to life in New York after the happenings of Spider-Man: No Way Home. Tom Holland reprises his role as the iconic web-slinger who confronts fresh dangers while managing the repercussions of his changed situation. 
 
This film blends superhero action with Peter's individual hardships. The cast includes Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Sadie Sink, Mark Ruffalo, and Jon Bernthal, among others. 
 
Drishyam: The Conclusion
 
Release Date: November 27 
Platform: Netflix
 
Ajay Devgn reprises his role as Vijay Salgaonkar in Drishyam: The Conclusion, the latest installment of the Hindi crime-thriller series. Under the direction of Abhishek Pathak, the story continues Vijay's ongoing struggle to protect his family and keep their secrets sealed. 
 
A new inquiry spearheaded by SP Rajveer Singh Tomar, portrayed by Jaideep Ahlawat, places additional strain on the Salgaonkar family. The cast also includes Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Prakash Raj, Ishita Dutta, and Mrunal Jadhav.
 
Supergirl
 
Reported Release Date: November 26
 
Platform: JioHotstar
 
DC's Supergirl centers around Kara Zor-El, portrayed by Milly Alcock, as she transforms her personal loss into a broader battle for justice. While traveling on her birthday, Kara meets a girl named Ruthye, who has just lost her father to a ruthless outlaw. 
 
After Kara’s dog Krypto is poisoned, she partners with Ruthye to seek vengeance and find a cure. Directed by Craig Gillespie, the film features performances from Eve Ridley and Matthias Schoenaerts.
 
Delhi 2021
 
Release Date: November 25
 
Platform: ZEE5
 
Delhi 2021 is a film that unfolds during the devastating second wave of the COVID-19 outbreak in the capital city of India. The narrative centers on Manjot, portrayed by Richa Chadha, who is a nurse at SL Criticare Hospital as the city battles a lack of hospital beds and medical oxygen supplies. 
 
As the strain on healthcare professionals escalates, she battles to rescue her patients while facing the emotional and professional impacts of the ongoing emergency.

data.title: Gold loans grow 60% Y-o-Y, women and tier-3 borrowers drive demand: CRIF
data.description:
Gold loans sustained strong growth momentum at 60 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y), a report from CRIF India shows. Active loans grew at a more moderate 14 per cent Y-o-Y, but growth accelerated from September 2025 levels of 10.7 per cent Y-o-Y. The portfolio-at-risk in the 31–90 days segment improved was flat at 1.3 per cent, but in the 91-80 day segment it improved by 30 basis points to 0.4 per cent.
 
Furthermore, gold-loan borrowers grew at a 15.6 per cent 3-year CAGR, indicating that broader portfolio growth has also been supported by increasing borrowers. Women borrowers and those from tier-3 markets are some of the faster-growing segments.

data.title: Deepika Padukone, Ranveer's parents ink 2 Bandra lease deals worth ₹10 cr
data.description:
Ranveer Singh's parents, Jugjeet Singh Bhavnani and Anju Bhavnani, along with actor Deepika Padukone and associated entities, have registered two 99-year lease deeds with Sagar Resham Co-operative Housing Society in Bandra West, Mumbai. Registration records accessed by Liases Foras show a consideration of ₹5 crore against each deed.
 
Both deeds were registered on 17 November 2026. The first was executed in April 2026, and a late-registration fine was paid on it. The deeds give the lessees exclusive use of specified areas and access rights at the society on Byramjee Jeejeebhoy Road, Bandstand, according to property documents accessed by Liases Foras.
 
The first deed covers the terrace above the 19th floor (about 2,045 sq ft), a swimming pool and exercise facilities to be built there by the lessees, and an exclusive lift. It runs for 99 years from 1 April 2026 and includes a ₹2 crore interest-free security deposit, refundable at the end of the lease.
 
 
The second deed records a non-refundable premium of ₹5 crore for additional exclusive areas, for 99 years from 13 November 2026. It grants a right of way over a 151.60 sq m strip of land from Byramjee Jeejeebhoy Road. It also allows common areas already allotted to the lessees to be converted using surplus FSI, subject to MCGM approval, with all costs borne by the lessees.
 
The lessees are KA Enterprises LLP, Anju Jugjeetsingh Bhavnani, KA Family Trust through trustee Deepika Padukone, Deepika Padukone individually, and Oh Five Oh Media Works LLP. Jugjeet Singh Bhavnani signed for Oh Five Oh Media Works LLP and, under a power of attorney, on Deepika Padukone's behalf.
 
The society's special general body meeting on 12 November 2026 unanimously approved leasing the additional areas for 99 years and authorised office-bearers to seek municipal permissions.

data.title: Average credit card transaction size falls 13% to ₹3,585 in Oct: CareEdge
data.description:
The average credit card transaction size declined 13.3 per cent to ₹3,585 in October 2026 from ₹4,133 a year ago, indicating more frequent use for smaller-value purchases, even as spending hit a record ₹2.45 trillion, according to a report by CareEdge Ratings.
 
The decline in transaction size came alongside a 31.8 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) increase in the number of credit card transactions to 68.3 crore during the month. Spending, meanwhile, grew 14.3 per cent during the month, while spending per card increased 2.9 per cent to ₹19,366, marking its first Y-o-Y rise since June 2026.
 
According to the report, the decline in average transaction size is partly due to the shift in the festive calendar. Last year, consumers made large in-store purchases, including jewellery and electronics, around Dhanteras and Diwali in October. This year, these purchases are expected to be reflected in November, as the festivals moved to that month.
 
 
The growing use of credit cards on the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), where transactions are typically of smaller value, could also be keeping the average ticket size lower, the report said.
 
The shift was also evident in the composition of card spending. Online transactions grew 22.6 per cent Y-o-Y in October, while point-of-sale (PoS) spending increased by just 2.5 per cent. Consequently, online spending accounted for 62.88 per cent of total credit card expenditure, compared with 58.62 per cent a year earlier.
 
Online festive sales began on October 8 this year, compared with September 23 last year, resulting in a shift in spending between the two months. Meanwhile, in-store purchases around Dhanteras and Diwali moved to November.
 
Banks added 14.01 lakh credit cards during October, taking the outstanding card base to 12.67 crore, up 11.1 per cent Y-o-Y. This was the fastest growth since November 2024 and the highest monthly addition since January 2024.
 
Public sector banks (PSBs) gained market share in credit card spending, with their share rising to 21.84 per cent in October from 20.41 per cent in September. Private sector banks' share declined to 72.65 per cent from 73.78 per cent.
 
“Banks are competing hard through card discounts and new issuance, and cards are being used more often, though for smaller payments,” said Saurabh Bhalerao, director, CareEdge Ratings.
 
The agency expects credit card spending to moderate to ₹2.07-2.23 trillion in November as online festive sales conclude. However, Dhanteras- and Diwali-related purchases are expected to keep spending above the level recorded in the corresponding month last year. It also cautioned that retail inflation above 6 per cent and higher interest rates could weigh on spending after the festive season.
